children: By Sukanya Mitra
Gold prices steadied on Wednesday after falling more than 2% in the previous session, as investors awaited US inflation data due later in the day for clues on the Federal Reserve's policy path.
Spot gold
was little changed at $3,558.85 per ounce by 0312 GMT. Prices had hit a 14-month low on Friday. US gold futures
for December delivery dropped 0.1% to $3,557.80.

"The recent decline was mainly driven by a selloff in the equity market because investors needed cash to pay for margin calls. As of now, markets continue to remain in consolidation mode until further signals," said ANZ analyst Soni Kumari.
Asian stocks tumbled as fresh US tariff threats hit sentiment and a tech-led rally fizzled, with the region's chip-heavy markets bearing the brunt of the selloff.
The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Index, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2% inflation rate, is due at 1330 GMT.
Markets are pricing in a 96.4% chance of a 25-basis-point rate increase at the Fed’s December policy meeting and a 3.6% probability of a larger 50-bp hike, according to CME’s FedWatch tool.
Higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.

US consumer confidence increased more than expected in November, touching its highest level in nearly two years, amid optimism over labour market conditions and the overall economy following this month's midterm elections.
"We expect gold's downward pressure to eventually reverse, although the recovery could remain muted into early 2027 before gaining momentum," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

Elsewhere, the World Gold Council said on Tuesday its Wholesale Digital Gold Initiative completed live pilot transactions under a new settlement model that enables electronic ownership and transfer of physical gold.
Among other metals, spot silver
steadied at $40.89 per ounce, platinum
slid 1% to $1,263.62 and palladium
